Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a small, hyperlucent right lung with ipsilateral mediastinal shift and a diminutive right hilum/pulmonary artery, which are classic radiographic features of hypogenetic lung syndrome (Scimitar syndrome). This congenital anomaly explains the patient's history of recurrent infections and stridor, whereas Swyer-James syndrome is typically post-infectious and unilateral absence of the pulmonary artery usually presents with a normal-sized lung.
